title: A Study of Imlunestrant (LY3484356) in Healthy Female Participants
official: A Phase 1, Open-Label, 4-Part Study to Investigate the Relative Bioavailability and Bioequivalence of Imlunestrant (LY3484356) Test and Reference Formulations and the Effects of Food and Omeprazole on the Pharmacokinetics of Imlunestrant, in Healthy Female Participants of Non-Childbearing Potential
summary:
The main purpose of this study is to measure the amount of imlunestrant that gets into the bloodstream and how long it takes the body to get rid of it when given in two different formulations. This study also compares the two different formulations of imlunestrant against the effects of food and omeprazole in the body.

For each participant, the study may last up to 2.5 months and participants can expect to stay in the clinical research unit (CRU) up to 27 days over several visits.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Are overtly healthy
* Have a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 18.0 to 35.0 kilograms per square meter (kg/m²)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Have known allergies to imlunestrant (freebase) or or imlunestrant tosylate or omeprazole
* Have significant history or clinical manifestation of an of the following disorders: metabolic, allergic, dermatological, hepatic, renal, hematological, pulmonary, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, neurological, respiratory, endocrine, or psychiatric
* Have a chronic history of liver disease, or known hepatic or biliary abnormalities
* Have a history of significant hypersensitivity, intolerance, or allergy to any drug compound, food, or other substance
* Have a clinically significant abnormality of blood pressure or pulse rate
* Have a history of alcoholism or drug/chemical abuse within 2 years prior to starting study
* Have alcohol intake that exceeds recommended average weekly alcohol consumption limits per local regulation, or an amount deemed significant by the investigator
* Have a positive ethanol breath/urine test result or positive urine drug screen
* Show evidence of hepatitis B, positive hepatitis B core antibody, or positive hepatitis B surface antigen
* Have a positive hepatitis C Virus (HCV) antibody test
* Have evidence of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection or positive HIV antibodies
* Smoke more than 10 cigarettes or use the equivalent tobacco, smoking-cessation products, nicotine-containing products, or e-cigarettes (nicotine and non-nicotine) per day
* Have received blood products within 2 months prior to check-in on Study Day -1
* Have donated blood within 3 months prior to screening, plasma within 2 weeks prior to screening, or platelets within 6 weeks prior to screening
